requirement_text: Information for citizens of a non-EU country who reside outside Italy and do not have an EU equivalent qualification. [...] You have a study path dedicated to you if: you are eligible for equal treatment as an EU citizen; you participate in the Marco Polo programme.
researcher_notes: Confirms two named dedicated tracks within the non-EU applicant category: 'equal treatment as an EU citizen' status (a recognized exception class, not detailed further on this page) and the Marco Polo programme -- the same named Chinese-student-specific government programme referenced independently at Politecnico di Torino (which gave a concrete Gao Kao minimum score of 400 specifically for Marco Polo students), confirming it as a real, national, cross-institutional track rather than one university's own scheme.

requirement_text: The CISIA tests (TOLC and CEnT-S) are required to apply to many restricted-access degree programmes and are also used by some open-access degree programmes to assess basic knowledge and assign any Additional Learning Requirements (OFA).
researcher_notes: Generalizes the OFA (Additional Learning Requirements) mechanism already found at Politecnico di Milano to a second Italian institution, and clarifies its dual purpose: the SAME CISIA test (TOLC/CEnT-S) functions as a hard admission gate for restricted-access programmes, but only as a diagnostic (determining OFA assignment, not admission itself) for open-access programmes -- a real structural difference in what a passing/failing score means depending on the programme's admission type, not reducible to one threshold semantics across the whole university.
